title: Idempotent policy apply API + webhook-driven Optimize rollout
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Redwood Optimize currently generates batching/caching recommendations but lacks a safe, observable automation path for applying those recommendations programmatically. Teams want an API + SDK that can 1) apply configuration changes idempotently, 2) emit webhook events for rollout status, and 3) support automatic rollback on regressions. Without this, customers either apply suggestions manually (slow) or build brittle automation around non-idempotent endpoints (risking duplicate/partial changes).

Goal: Ship an API and SDK surface that enables automated Optimize workflows to safely apply, monitor, and (if necessary) rollback batching/caching and routing policies. The implementation must:
  - Guarantee idempotent apply semantics (client-supplied idempotency key + server-side dedup + stable operation IDs)
  - Provide a polling/status endpoint and a webhook stream with structured events for lifecycle states (queued, applying, applied, validation_failed, rolled_back, failed)
  - Support declarative policy payloads and a reversible change model (store prior config snapshots for rollback)
  - Integrate with existing rollout primitives (canary fraction, step delays, automatic quality gates)
  - Surface granular telemetry (tokens saved, latency/throughput effect estimates, confidence score) for audit and billing reconciliation

Proposed API summary (high level):
  - POST /v1/optimize/policies/apply
      - Headers: Authorization, Idempotency-Key
      - Body: {scope_id, policy_patch: <declarative-diff>, rollout: {mode: canary|immediate, fraction: 0-1, step_delay_seconds}, validation_prompts: [id], metadata: {reason, run_by}}
      - Response: 202 Accepted {operation_id, status_url}
  - GET /v1/optimize/operations/{operation_id}
      - Returns operation state, start/end timestamps, applied_changes, snapshot_id, validation_results
  - POST /v1/optimize/operations/{operation_id}/rollback
      - Body: {reason, force: boolean}
      - Response: 202 Accepted (initiates rollback)

Idempotency model:
  - Clients MUST send an Idempotency-Key header per logical apply attempt. Keys are scoped per-customer and expire after 72h of inactivity.
  - Server stores the final outcome (applied/failed/rolled_back) keyed by (customer_id, idempotency_key). Replaying the same key returns the same operation_id and final state once terminal.
  - If a previously-applied operation is retried with a changed payload, return 409 with existing operation_id and hint to create a new idempotency key.
  - Partial failures during rolling (network glitch, coordinator crash) must be recoverable: operation state is durable and reconciled by background workers.

Webhook contract:
  - Endpoint owners register webhook URLs in Console or via API. Events are JSON with a top-level type and operation_id. Example events: optimize.operation.queued, optimize.operation.started, optimize.operation.step_completed, optimize.operation.validation_failed, optimize.operation.applied, optimize.operation.rolled_back, optimize.operation.failed.
  - Payload includes: operation_id, scope_id, patch_summary (human-readable), snapshot_id (pre-change), metrics_delta_estimate, validation_results (if any), and timestamp.
  - Webhooks delivered at-least-once; include event_id and deduplication_hint. SDK to provide automatic ack/retry helpers.

Rollback semantics:
  - Every apply stores a full config snapshot (snapshot_id). Rollback re-applies snapshot_id as a new operation (with its own idempotency key optional).
  - Automatic rollback can be triggered by validation gates (e.g., quality metric drop > threshold) or external signals (customer cancel, alerting rules).
  - Rollback operations are recorded and exposed in operation history for audit.

SDK changes (Node/Python initially):
  - New clients.optimize.apply(policyPatch, {idempotencyKey, rollout, validationPrompts, metadata}) returns an Operation object with watch() helpers and on(event, cb) hooks mapped from webhooks.
  - Helpers for registering/consuming webhooks in local dev with signed payload verification utilities.
  - Utilities for generating stable idempotency keys (UUID v4 with prefix) and a recommended retry backoff strategy.

Acceptance criteria:
  - API endpoints implemented and documented in openapi.yaml with examples.
  - End-to-end integration test: create recommendation -> apply via API with idempotency key -> simulate a transient failure and re-send same key -> confirm single operation recorded and final outcome consistent.
  - Webhook event payloads conform to schema and retries are exercised.
  - SDK exposes the apply/watch/on primitives and passes integration tests.
  - Telemetry: operation duration, validation outcomes, metrics_delta_estimate recorded to observability (console) and surfaced in the operation detail page.

Security and privacy notes: objects may contain customer config; apply operations require stricter RBAC (only Optimize-automation role or higher). KMS keys used for signing webhook payloads. Security review required prior to release.

Migration/compatibility: support existing manual console flow unchanged; customers opting into automation must be granted a new API scope. Provide a one-click console UI to generate an idempotency example and test webhook endpoint.

Rollout plan:
  1) Internal alpha: run automation against internal staging org, smoke validate rollback and idempotency behavior (2 weeks).
  2) Beta: opt-in for selected customers (feature flag) with explicit support. Monitor regressions and telemetry (4 weeks).
  3) GA: general availability in optimize-2026.04 release after security review and docs.
updates: 2026-03-11: Initial design spike completed. Chosen model: client Idempotency-Key + server dedup store (redis w/ durable backup). Decision doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPT/Idempotent+Apply+Design (internal).

2026-03-12: POC: POST /v1/optimize/policies/apply created in feature branch feat/optimize/apply-api. Basic operation object persisted to operations table. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5872
2026-03-13: Discussed webhook delivery guarantees with infra. Using at-least-once + event_id for dedup. Added signing with HMAC-SHA256 and key rotation plan.

2026-03-14: QA wrote integration tests for idempotency replay and rollback. Found race where apply+rollback could interleave during canary steps; added coordinator mutex in redis to serialize operation state transitions (patch in PR 5895).
Next steps: finalize OpenAPI spec, publish SDK helpers, run alpha against staging, coordinate security review with Privacy & Sec teams.
